bottlenecks.reading: The scarce thing Google Cloud supplies is AI compute capacity (Google's own TPUs and GPUs, in powered data centers), and contracted demand exceeds what can be delivered. Alphabet reports $519.5 billion of revenue backlog at 2026-06-30, $513.9 billion of it Google Cloud, just over half to be recognized in the next 24 months; Alphabet itself says cloud revenue is affected by 'supply availability'. The rivals report the same shortage: Oracle states that customer demand for AI cloud training and inferencing 'continues to grow faster than supply' (RPO $664 billion at 2026-08-31); Microsoft's commercial RPO is $678 billion (+84%) and Amazon's performance obligations are about $496 billion (6.4-year weighted life) at 2026-06-30. The four disclosed backlogs total about $2.4 trillion but are different RPO definitions and dates, so they are not additive and show contracted demand, not Google's share. The shortage lasts at least as long as capacity is being delivered into the backlog (Alphabet: just over half within 24 months, the rest later). Capacity adders: Alphabet capex $44.9 billion in Q2 2026 ($80.6 billion H1, vs $39.6 billion H1 2025); Amazon purchases of property and equipment $54.2 billion in Q2; Microsoft $35.8 billion in FQ4 (FY26 $115.9 billion); Meta $34.9 billion in Q3 (FY26 guide $135-145 billion); Oracle $28.5 billion in Q1 FY27 with 850 MW delivered. Update for Jul-Sep 2026 (results day 2026-10-28): Alphabet purchases of property and equipment $51.4 billion in Q3 (vs $24.0 billion; nine months $132.0 billion vs $63.6 billion) while Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7 billion with TPU system sales 'a meaningful contributor' and segment operating margin 36.2% (vs 23.7%); Microsoft added $39.4 billion of property and equipment in FQ1 FY27 (vs $19.4 billion), Azure +48%, commercial RPO $677 billion (+73%); Oracle (Investor Day 2026-10-28) says its capex peaks in FY27-FY28 and steps down in FY29. Alphabet's Q3 Cloud backlog was not in the release text read (call not read by this lane): the $513.9 billion is still the latest backlog figure here.

Power and grid interconnection is the longest-lead input behind that capacity. Google's head of sustainability and climate policy said (Network World, 2026-01-15) that transmission is 'the number one challenge', that utilities in many markets quote four, five, sometimes ten years to interconnect, and one quoted 12 years just to study the request; the article also relays Berkeley Lab data that interconnection waits rose from under 2 years (projects built 2000-2007) to over 4 years (2018-2024). Alphabet's own filing shows the response: it closed the $5.9 billion Intersect (renewable energy developer) acquisition on 2026-03-10 to accelerate data center capacity and energy development, carries power purchase and energy agreements, and gave financial guarantees (maximum $7.6 billion) backstopping counterparties' long-lead power equipment. Who adds capacity: utilities and grid operators (slow, years), and the hyperscalers themselves by buying generation and co-locating; this favors the rivals with the most capital and existing powered sites, and is a cost and timing risk for Alphabet's capex plan.

Accelerator supply is the other scarce input, and Alphabet differs from the rivals by owning its own chip line. Alphabet began recognizing revenue from selling TPU systems to customers (on-premises, specialized high-scale workloads) in Q2 2026, with the significant majority to be recognized in 2027, and it has long-term supply agreements to secure future production capacity (third-party contract manufacturers); this adds cost and operational complexity, per the 10-Q. Amazon says its chips business has passed a $25 billion annual run rate, growing triple digits, with Anthropic and OpenAI making multi-year, multi-gigawatt Trainium commitments, so Google's TPU is no longer the only large in-house alternative to merchant GPUs. How long: the TPU product-sale revenue is mostly a 2027 item, so the shortage runs at least through 2027 on Alphabet's own timing.

Market direction and size: Synergy Research Group put worldwide cloud infrastructure services spending at $143 billion in Q2 2026 (about $500 billion trailing twelve months), up 43% year over year, the 11th successive quarter of accelerating growth, with generative AI named as the primary driver and public IaaS/PaaS growing 47%. This is an attributed industry study; it counts spending, not capacity, and is consistent with the three hyperscalers' own segment growth (AWS +37%, Google Cloud +82%, Microsoft Intelligent Cloud +32%, Azure and other cloud +43%, Oracle IaaS +121%) for Apr-Aug 2026.

fd SHARE CLOUD Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep, company-reported, USD m): Google Cloud 30,709 vs 15,157 (+102.6%, +15,552 y/y; segment operating margin 36.2% vs 23.7%) [pf_rel_20261028_1]; Microsoft Agents and Infra 76,795 vs 61,672 (+24.5%, +15,123; operating margin 52.8%; new FY27 segment, includes M365 commercial and server products, not comparable to Google Cloud), Azure growth +48% (no dollar figure), Microsoft Cloud 63.9bn +30% [fd_msft_rel_20261028]. Google Cloud's growth rate accelerated from +82% (Q2) to +103% (Q3) while Azure went from +43% (Azure and other cloud, FQ4) to +48%; Google Cloud added about the same absolute dollars in the quarter as Microsoft's whole Agents and Infra segment. Part of Google's acceleration is TPU system product sales (first recognized Q2 2026; dollar amount not split out in the release), which AWS and Azure do not sell as hardware, so growth rates are not like for like. AWS Q3 not yet reported (gap).

fd SHARE ADVERTISING Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep, USD m, derived from own releases, NOT market share): Google advertising 82,012 vs 74,182 (+10.6%; Search & other 63,350 +12.0%, YouTube ads 11,207 +9.2%, Network 7,455 +1.4%) [pf_rel_20261028_1]; Meta advertising 63,061 vs 50,082 (+25.9%) [fd_meta_rel_20261021]; Microsoft search and advertising ex-TAC +12% [fd_msft_rel_20261028]. fd SHARE CLOUD ATTRIBUTED (Synergy Research Group, 2026-07-30, fd_synergy_20260730): worldwide cloud infrastructure services Q2 2026 share Amazon 28%, Microsoft 20%, Google 15% on a $143 billion quarter (+43% y/y). The page read does not state prior-year shares. HYPOTHESIS, not verified against Synergy's own release: trade press relaying the same data reports Q2 2025 shares of Amazon 30%, Microsoft 20%, Google 13% and calls 15% a record for Google; if right, Google gained about 2 points and Amazon lost about 2 points in a year, consistent with the segment growth rates above (82% vs 37% vs 32%).

fd SHARE ADVERTISING (calendar H1 2026 vs H1 2025, USD m, derived from the companies' own releases; NOT market share): Google advertising 158,882 vs 138,225 (+14.9%) [pf_rel_20260722_1, pf_rel_20260429_1: Search & other 123,670 +17.9%, YouTube ads 20,938 +11.8%, Network 14,274 -2.3%]; Meta advertising 114,388 vs 87,955 (+30.1%) [fd_meta_rel_20261021: nine months 177,449 minus Q3 63,061; 2025 138,037 minus 50,082]; Amazon advertising 37,052 vs 29,615 (+25.1%) [fd_amzn_rel_20260730]. Among these three alone Google's slice moved from 54.0% to 51.2% (-2.8 points), Meta 34.4% to 36.9%, Amazon 11.6% to 11.9%. Read: Google's advertising is growing, Search is accelerating inside it, but Meta and Amazon are growing about twice as fast on a smaller base, so Google is losing relative share of this three-company pool. Caveats: excludes Microsoft/LinkedIn, TikTok, Apple, traditional media; Google's total includes Network (partner sites, shrinking); the pool is the three companies' reported revenue, not an advertiser-budget market. Context: Meta Q3 2026 advertising +25.9% (impressions +10%, price per ad +14%) [fd_meta_rel_20261021]; Amazon Q2 advertising +26.2% [fd_amzn_rel_20260730]; Google Q2 advertising +14.4% (Search & other +16.8%, YouTube +12.9%, Network -0.7%) [pf_rel_20260722_1].

fd SHARE SEARCH (StatCounter, fd_statcounter_202609): worldwide search engine share September 2026 Google 89.94%, Bing 5.29%, Yahoo 1.36%, Yandex 1.3%, DuckDuckGo 0.74%, Baidu 0.44%. The page shows no prior-year month. HYPOTHESIS from secondary blogs not read at source: StatCounter-based figures of about 90.0% (April), 90.4% (May) and 91.3% (June 2026) for Google. Either way Google's share of referral-based search is roughly flat near 90%; Microsoft's own report shows Bing/search advertising ex-TAC +10% in Apr-Jun 2026 against Google Search & other +16.8%. StatCounter does not count AI assistants, so it cannot show share lost to them.

fd SHARE AI ASSISTANTS: no primary source read. Secondary marketing-blog figures (Similarweb June 2026: ChatGPT about 55% and Gemini about 27% of web visits across a seven-app set; StatCounter May 2026: ChatGPT 79%) disagree by tracker and are HYPOTHESIS only; OpenAI and Anthropic are private so no audited numbers exist. Alphabet's own reading: all 15 of its half-billion-user products, seven with two billion users, use Gemini (10-K Item 1, pf_10k_20260205); Alphabet Q2 release says nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 use Gemini Enterprise (pf_rel_20260722_1).

fd COOPETITION: the frontier labs are customers or investees of Google's cloud rivals. Amazon's Q2 2026 release books $53.4 billion of non-operating income 'primarily from our investments in Anthropic' and says Anthropic and OpenAI each made multi-year, multi-gigawatt Trainium commitments [fd_amzn_rel_20260730]; Microsoft's FQ4 release reports a $3.2 billion gain from its Anthropic investment and separately adjusts for its OpenAI investments [fd_msft_rel_20260729]; Oracle's RPO growth is described as AI-contract driven [fd_orcl_rel_20260910]. Amazon's Bedrock lists Google DeepMind's Gemma 4 alongside GPT-5.6 and Claude Opus 5. Alphabet's Q2 2026 net gains on equity securities of $99.0 billion are described as unrealized gains 'from SpaceX and a private company' [pf_rel_20260722_1, pf_10q_20260723]; no Alphabet document read here names Anthropic or OpenAI.

fd MARGIN AND CAPITAL COMPARISON (latest quarter, company-reported): operating margin Alphabet Q2 2026 34.0% (Google Cloud segment 35.6%) [pf_rel_20260722_1]; Microsoft FQ4 45.1%; Amazon Q2 13.7% (AWS 39.4%); Meta Q3 20.1% GAAP / 35.4% ex a $9.89 billion legal charge; Oracle Q1 FY27 34.8%. Rivals' free cash flow turned thin or negative on AI capex: Amazon TTM free cash flow -$7.6 billion, Meta Q3 -$2.1 billion, Oracle Q1 -$5 billion; Meta is creating a new non-voting Class C share class (effective January 2027) to raise capital and pay for acquisitions and compensation; Alphabet raised $49.6 billion net equity (June 2026, common and mandatory convertible preferred) and $20.3 billion of notes in Q2 2026 to fund AI infrastructure [pf_10q_20260723]. The sector is funding capacity with outside capital, which links the field's growth to financing and holder dilution.
